correctness.rationale: Antipodal pair obstruction yields the exact minimum, transversals strongly resolve by an explicit antipodal geodesic, and a coordinate-half-cube supplies hop feasibility. Dimension-five Clebsch incidence has the independently reconstructed face vector (1,16,80,160,80,16). Dimension six splits into two parity-side 16-pair choices with precisely 32 forbidden stars per side. For \(d\ge8\), events of full closed distance-two neighborhoods have first Bonferroni mass \(2^{d-m-1}\); distance-two center pairs uniquely contribute \(m2^{3d-2m-5}\), all other pairs sum at most \(2^{2d-2m+3}\), and triples at most \(2^{9d-3m-9}\). The two error terms are little-o of the second term. Exact finite programs rebuild all relevant graph structures and match the written proof; no finite computation is used to establish the infinite claim.

value.rationale: The core gap is the configuration count of optimum sets satisfying two independent geometric constraints, not the already-known minimum strong-metric number. On the canonical infinite binary cube family, hop feasibility removes an exponentially tiny but structurally correlated subset of antipodal transversals. The exact six-dimensional boundary count and sharp two-order asymptotic identify the first obstruction and its pair-interaction coefficient; the explicit smaller error is stronger than a routine union bound. This provides an interpretable all-dimension census estimate and reproduces the covered five-dimensional special case with accurate attribution.
